market_context: U.S. futures indicate a muted, mixed open: S&P 500 futures were approximately 0.05%-0.10% higher, while Nasdaq 100 futures were approximately 0.10%-0.22% lower.[2][4] Brent crude traded above $106 per barrel amid Middle East supply concerns, supporting energy shares but potentially increasing inflation and interest-rate pressure.[4][5] Investors are positioned cautiously ahead of major-bank earnings beginning Tuesday and September CPI on Wednesday.[2][4]

predictions.reasoning: S&P 500 futures were modestly positive and the index recently posted a record-setting week, suggesting limited upside follow-through despite a muted open.[2][5] Strong expected third-quarter earnings growth provides support, while elevated oil prices and upcoming CPI limit conviction.[4]

Nasdaq 100 futures were down approximately 0.10%-0.22% before the open, contrasting with slightly firmer S&P and Dow futures.[2][3][4] Higher oil prices and the possibility of renewed inflation-driven rate pressure create a relative headwind for long-duration technology shares.[4]

Exxon Mobil was reported approximately 1.2% higher in premarket trading as Brent crude moved above $106 per barrel.[5] Continued geopolitical supply disruption is a direct near-term catalyst for integrated oil producers, though price volatility remains elevated.[4]

The technology complex faced mild premarket pressure, with Nasdaq futures lower and Micron down more than 2% after reported advances by Chinese memory maker CXMT.[1][4] That semiconductor-specific sentiment could weigh on NVDA, although strong expected technology-sector earnings limits downside confidence.[4]
